commonProblems.h2: Iveco S-Way Engine Problems - What It Costs to Fix & When Replacement Makes Sense
commonProblems.h3: The Iveco S-Way, launched in 2019, is powered by the FPT Cursor engine family-specifically the Cursor 9 (8.7L), Cursor 11 (11.1L), and Cursor 13 (12.9L)-with the 12.9L Cursor 13 in 460hp, 500hp, 530hp, and 570hp outputs dominating replacement demand. While these are fundamentally robust heavy-duty engines, certain failure patterns have emerged across the S-Way range, particularly around emissions systems, turbocharger components, and cooling system integrity. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EngineMarket includes upgraded internal components designed to address the original failure point-plus a minimum 12‑month unlimited mileage warranty. Below, we break down the most common Iveco S-Way engine problems by failure type, with realistic UK cost comparisons so you can decide whether repair or replacement makes sense for your truck.

problems.h4: Iveco S-Way AdBlue System Failure - Why Euro 6d Emissions Logic Causes Torque Derate
problems.affectedModels: Iveco S-Way all variants (2019-present) with Cursor 9, Cursor 11, and Cursor 13 Euro 6d engines; most acute on 2022-2024 models
problems.rootCause: On Iveco S-Way Euro 6d models, emissions strategies are exceptionally strict. The slightest SCR or NOx inconsistency triggers rapid inducement-torque reduction, speed limitation, or complete immobilisation. The HI-eSCR system (used on approximately 95% of S-Way heavy models) continuously monitors NOx sensors, temperatures, and pressures via CAN bus. Any signal inconsistency triggers engine protection strategies. Faults often return after clearing because the logic remains active. AdBlue pump failures, NOx sensor faults, and SCR catalyst efficiency issues are the primary culprits.
problems.recommendation: On a 2022+ Iveco S-Way with 50,000-150,000 km, a specialist-led SCR component replacement is often the most cost-effective route-provided the engine itself hasn't suffered internal damage from prolonged derate operation. However, if the truck has been running in limp mode for extended periods or has logged multiple recurring AdBlue faults, the emissions system contamination may have compromised the engine internals. In those cases, we recommend a full rebuilt engine with upgraded components. For a 2022 S-Way 530 worth £35,000-£45,000, investing £7,500-£12,000 in a warranted replacement engine often makes better commercial sense than chasing recurring emissions faults.
problems.cta: Compare rebuilt Cursor 13 engine prices for your Iveco S-Way

problems.group: Iveco S-Way Turbocharger Actuator & VGT Failure
problems.h4: Iveco S-Way Turbocharger Actuator & VGT Failure - Why Cursor Engines Lose Boost
problems.affectedModels: Iveco S-Way all variants (2019-present) with Cursor 9, Cursor 11, and Cursor 13 engines; particularly common on 2020-2023 models
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 80,000 - 250,000 km; some failures reported as early as 50,000 km
problems.rootCause: The variable geometry turbocharger (VGT) on Cursor engines suffers from sticking variable vanes due to soot accumulation, and vacuum actuator failure. The turbocharger actuator relies on vacuum pressure to control boost; when the actuator sticks or the vacuum system leaks, boost pressure drops, triggering power loss and excessive smoke. Poor maintenance and improper engine shutdown after high-load operation (which causes turbo overheating) accelerate failure.
problems.recommendation: If you catch turbo actuator failure early-before the variable vanes seize or the turbo ingests debris-a specialist actuator or VGT rebuild is a sound investment. However, on higher-mileage S-Way units (150,000+ km) where the turbo has been running poorly for some time, the risk of downstream engine damage is significant. For a 2021 S-Way 500 with 200,000 km, we recommend a full rebuilt engine with an upgraded turbocharger-the peace of mind and warranty coverage outweigh the marginal cost difference versus a standalone turbo replacement that may not address underlying wear.
problems.cta: Compare Iveco S-Way turbocharger repair vs replacement costs

problems.group: Iveco S-Way Cursor 13 EGR Cooler Fouling
problems.h4: Iveco S-Way Cursor 13 EGR Cooler Fouling - Why Euro V and Early Euro VI Engines Lose Power
problems.affectedModels: Iveco S-Way with Cursor 13 Euro V and early Euro VI engines (2019-2021); less prevalent on post-2022 models with updated calibration
problems.rootCause: Under specific low-load, low-temperature operating conditions, the EGR cooler on Cursor 13 engines can become fouled with soot and carbon deposits, as documented in IVECO Service Information Bulletin SI 13‑045. This reduces cooling efficiency and increases DPF regeneration frequency. On Euro V models (pre-2014, carried over into some early S-Way production), the issue is more acute; post-2014 Euro VI models benefit from updated calibration and maintenance protocols.
problems.recommendation: On a 2019-2021 S-Way Cursor 13 with EGR cooler fouling, a specialist EGR cooler replacement is the sensible first step-provided the engine hasn't been overheated. However, if the truck has been running with reduced power for an extended period or has logged multiple DPF regeneration issues, the engine may have sustained internal wear. In those cases, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components offers better long-term value. For a 2020 S-Way 530 worth £30,000-£40,000, a £7,500-£12,000 warranted replacement engine is a commercially sound decision.
problems.cta: Get a quote for Iveco S-Way Cursor 13 engine replacement

problems.group: Iveco S-Way Engine Oil Leak & Coolant Loss
problems.h4: Iveco S-Way Engine Oil Leak & Coolant Loss - Why S-Way 500 Full Plus Engines Fail Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Iveco S-Way 500 Full Plus and 530 Full Plus (2022-2024 models); reported on Cursor 13 engines with 43,000-80,000 km
problems.typicalFailureMileage: As low as 14,000 km; commonly reported between 43,000-80,000 km
problems.rootCause: Multiple owner reports document S-Way 500 Full Plus and 530 Full Plus vehicles developing oil and coolant leaks at very low mileage. In some cases, engine locking has been reported at just 14,000 km. The root causes appear to include oil seal failures, cylinder head cracking (particularly on early Cursor 11 builds), and cooling system stress under heavy load. Radiator and coolant leaks are common, and if not addressed promptly, overheating can cause catastrophic engine damage.
problems.recommendation: On a 2022-2024 S-Way 500 or 530 Full Plus with oil or coolant loss, time is of the essence. If caught before the oil pressure warning light illuminates, a specialist seal and gasket replacement may resolve the issue. However, once the oil pressure light comes on-or worse, the engine locks-the internal damage is almost certainly terminal. For a 2022 S-Way 530 worth £35,000-£45,000, we strongly recommend a full rebuilt engine. The cost of a replacement is significantly less than the downtime, lost revenue, and potential write-off of a truck with a seized engine.

problems.group: Iveco S-Way Cursor 11 Cylinder Head Cracking
problems.h4: Iveco S-Way Cursor 11 Cylinder Head Cracking - Why LNG and Early Diesel Engines Fail Under Load
problems.affectedModels: Iveco S-Way with Cursor 11 engines (including LNG F3HFE601A and diesel variants); early production 2019-2021 most affected
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 80,000 - 200,000 km; more common under continuous high-load, high-ambient-temperature operations
problems.rootCause: Early Cursor 11 engines experienced localised overheating in the cylinder head under extreme continuous load. The primary reliability focus for the Cursor 11 is managing thermal stress in the cylinder head, with elevated incidence in continuous high-load, high-ambient-temperature operations. This can lead to cylinder head cracking and EGR cooler internal leaks.
problems.recommendation: On a 2019-2021 S-Way Cursor 11 (including LNG variants), a specialist cylinder head replacement is a viable option if the bottom end is sound. However, given the known thermal stress issues on early Cursor 11 builds, we recommend a full rebuilt engine with upgraded components-particularly for LNG-powered S-Way trucks operating in long-haul, high-load applications. The additional cost is justified by the warranty coverage and the elimination of underlying design weaknesses.

items.question: What engine is in the Iveco S-Way?
items.answer: The Iveco S-Way is powered by FPT Industrial Cursor engines - the 8.7L Cursor 9, 11.1L Cursor 11, and 12.9L Cursor 13 - in diesel and LNG/CNG natural gas variants.

items.question: Is the Iveco S-Way Cursor 13 engine reliable?
items.answer: The Cursor 13 is generally robust - Iveco claims a 1.6 million km design life - but UK fleet operators report specific issues including turbo actuator failures, EGR cooler fouling, and oil/coolant leaks, particularly on higher-mileage units.

items.question: What are the most common Iveco S-Way engine problems?
items.answer: The most frequently reported S-Way engine issues are AdBlue system failures, turbocharger actuator/VTG problems, cooling system leaks, oil leaks, and - in severe cases - engine seizure at surprisingly low mileages.

items.question: How long does an Iveco S-Way engine last?

items.question: What causes Iveco S-Way engine failure?
items.answer: The most common failure causes are AdBlue system neglect (causing SCR derate), turbocharger actuator carbon buildup, oil/coolant leaks leading to lubrication failure, and - on some 530 models - catastrophic internal failure at around 110,000 km.
